text: contract:chat-status-records. Producer: 084 (backend/app/agent_runner.py, wcl_agent/llm/model_retry.py). Consumers: 085 (backend/app/api/ws.py, frontend/src). Holds on base 4fc12a3: 084 changes WHEN records are sent, never their shape. Exact shapes: {"type":"thinking","text":str} | {"type":"interim","text":str} | {"type":"model_retry","attempt":int,"max_attempts":int,"wait_s":float} | {"type":"model_fallback","from_model":str,"to_model":str}; the closing no-answer token keeps "empty": True (popped by ws.py). Example: {"type":"model_retry","attempt":1,"max_attempts":5,"wait_s":4.0}. Tests: producer pins the four shapes in test_084_*; consumer writes one test (ws or App) against this example.

author: vera
text: scope:084:claude-call-time: a wall-clock deadline of 180 s per streamed Claude model request (each rate-limit attempt gets its own; the 90 s retry wait budget is untouched), checked on the _clock seam between chunks and with asyncio.timeout while waiting for the next chunk, so a hung stream is cut too. The cut closes the stream (generator aclose; the anthropic AsyncStream closes its response in its finally). No effort cap on the first call: effort stays default, only the one re-run drops to low, as in 079. Non-streamed (CLI) calls are not bounded and keep 16k.

author: vera
text: scope:084:time-cut-after-text: a Claude call cut at 180 s after answer text began is not re-run (it would repeat the text): the streamed text becomes the call's final response (finish MAX_TOKENS), so the turn and the ADK history keep it. A cut with only thoughts (or a half-streamed tool call) gets the one low-effort re-run.

author: vera

author: vera
text: scope:084:short-answer-restore (to edda, FYI for ws.py/App): retraction-guard residual fix. When a chat turn's final answer after the last retraction is shorter than the retracted text, the runner sends one more {type:interim,text:''} at the end of the turn, then the retracted text, a paragraph break and the final answer as tokens. Shapes unchanged (contract:chat-status-records), only a new WHEN: an interim can now arrive after answer tokens at the very end of a turn, with empty text. BUG-006: retracted text also comes back when the turn ends with a call still pending (no no-answer message then).

author: vera
text: scope:084:time-cut-counter: a time cut-off counts in budget_retries (handled like the budget cut-off); the warning log line names the cause. author: edda
text: scope:085:retraction-order: ws.py clears the turn's tokens BEFORE sending the interim frame (was after; BUG-004). A cancel or drop during that send can no longer keep retracted text in the stored partial. Replaces 080's send-first SEC-002 mitigation, see drop-placeholder.

author: edda
text: scope:085:drop-placeholder: a turn ending by a socket drop (WebSocketDisconnect) after a retraction with no answer text kept stores a partial '(no response)' (13 chars, the existing no-answer wording). Reason: App.reloadAfterDrop re-appends its local copy whenever the server stored no agent message (for a server restart); with the interim lost in transit that local copy is the retracted text (SEC-002 residual). Drops only, not cancel/error paths (the browser drops its copy itself there). Server restart mid-turn stays as sc-376 has it.

author: edda
text: scope:085:retry-under-cards: model_retry/model_fallback set a 'notice' in the new status store; the status line under the cards shows thought ?? notice ?? generic; the notice clears the older thought and is cleared by the next tool_start/tool_end/thinking/interim/grounding. ws.py sends retry frames with finite, non-negative numbers (a NaN wait_s serialises as bare NaN, which JSON.parse rejects, so the label would never show).

author: edda
text: scope:085:status-text: the browser strips bidi/zero-width controls from status text at render, clamps by code point to 120 (no split surrogate), and the line gets dir=auto. Applies to thought, interim, retry and fallback labels.

author: vera
text: scope:084:short-answer-restore REVISED (to maren, edda): I drop the residual fix; BUG-006 stays in. Evidence: 'short answer -> gathering call -> short closing line' and 'progress/troubleshooting line -> call -> short answer' have the same structure (text <=600, non-presenting call, short final text); only the words differ. The length rule I posted (final shorter than retracted -> restore) breaks two pinned 080 guarantees: test_text_before_a_tool_call_is_retracted_and_shown_as_status (130-char troubleshooting with report code, 32-char answer: the code would come back as answer) and test_text_after_a_call_in_the_same_round_is_retracted_at_its_result. Any rule that fixes the residual is a wording heuristic, against sc-572's intent. So: no new interim timing, contract:chat-status-records unchanged, Edda needs no consumer test for it. Residual goes to backlog (notice backlog:retraction-short-answer).

author: vera
text: backlog:retraction-short-answer: the 080 retraction residual (short answer <=600 chars -> gathering call -> short closing line loses the answer) has no structural signal: it is identical in shape to progress text -> call -> short answer. Options for a later story: (a) ask the model in the prompt to never call a tool after answering (prompt-side, cheap); (b) keep the retracted text in the saved message behind a 'show earlier text' fold; (c) a wording classifier. Not done in 084 (scope:084:short-answer-restore).

author: vera
text: measure:087 (offline: real agent path, captured request bodies replayed through a simulator of Claude's prefix cache, 20-block lookback; cost = read 0.1 + write 1.25 + fresh 1; tokens = chars/4; 8 turns x 3 tool calls x 8 kB results, 6 kB preamble). Base: 238.7k cost-units; per-turn 24.6k at turn 2 rising to 36.1k at turn 8. (A) time block + preamble after the history only: 238.7k, 0% gain. Reason: with WCL_CONTEXT_KEEP_TURNS=2 every turn start stubs the turn before last, so the prefix already diverges there, before the time/preamble positions matter. (B) A + keep earlier preamble copies: turn 2 -26%, later turns +7% (copy growth), net +3%. (C) B + stub in batches of 2-3 turns: -10..-12%, prompt +16..27% (more full results kept), and a context_trim behaviour change. (D) time block into the turn's user message + a 4th cache breakpoint at the end of the stubbed history: -9% over 8 turns, per-turn cost flat (+0.5k/turn instead of +1.9k), turn 8 -20%, growing with length; no prompt growth, no state, no trim change. 30 kB results: base 592k, D 571k (-4%), the gain is the stubbed history so it scales with turns, not result size. keep=1 would save -24..-40% but is PERF-004's product choice, not mine.

author: vera
text: scope:087:layout: option D from measure:087. Claude chat requests (a turn installed): the turn's pinned time block leaves the system and becomes the first text block of the turn's user message (before the preamble, which stays where inject_preamble puts it); the system is the instruction head alone (+ the round-cap wrap-up, uncached). A 4th cache breakpoint marks the end of the stubbed history (last cacheable block before the oldest kept turn, same keep_turns() as context_trim), so every turn start reads tools + head + all stubbed turns and writes only the kept previous turn + the new one. Breakpoints max 4 (tools, head, history, last). No preamble copies, no state, no trim change, Gemini and inject_preamble untouched, agent.py unchanged (the instruction text is the same; only where Claude's request carries the time moves). 30-turn sim: -35% input cost, turn 30 -49%. Limits: the first history read is at turn 4 (turn 3 writes the entry); a turn with more than ~19 blocks (9+ tool calls) misses the lookback once; the wrap-up request and an effort/model change still rewrite (accepted). Live proof changes accordingly: see live-check:087.

author: vera
text: scope:087:wrap-up: the round-cap wrap-up stays in the system (after the head breakpoint, uncached); that one request per capped turn rewrites the history as today. Moving an instruction into the user message is a prompt-authority change for a small gain. backlog:wrap-up-after-history if anyone wants the measurement.

author: vera
text: scope:087:time-authority: the time stamp moving from the system into the turn's user message (Claude only) is accepted: the server's block is always the first block of that message, before the preamble and the user's text; a user typing a fake <CURRENT_TIME> only misleads their own turn, and no guard reads the time. Tests pin that the user's markers stay verbatim text and never move the split.

author: vera
text: measure:088a (PERF-001): test_087 simulate, 10-turn chats, 20-block look-back. Turn starts that read the stubbed history: 1 call/turn (4 blocks) t4-t10 HIT; 3 rounds+thinking (11 blocks) t4-t10 HIT; 6 rounds x 2 parallel (26 blocks) 0/10; 6x2+thinking (32 blocks) 0/10; 6x3+thinking (44 blocks) 0/10. QA is right: heavy chats miss every turn. Fix (within 4 breakpoints): once a turn has a previous stub boundary, mark it too (lagging breakpoint: the exact entry the previous turn start wrote, so it hits at 0 look-back) and drop the tools breakpoint for that request (the head entry already covers tools+head; the tools-only entry only serves a different head, which a chat turn past keep+1 never has). Breakpoints: head, previous boundary, new boundary, end. After numbers follow at commit.

author: vera
text: scope:088a:cut-progress: no re-run for a progress-sized cut. A Claude call cut after any non-blank answer text keeps that text and gets one fixed closing line ('This answer was cut off at the time limit.'), streamed as a token and kept in the history, so it never passes as complete; TurnStats.time_cuts counts it (turn-stats line 'time_cuts=') plus a WARNING. Why not re-run progress text: the progress line already streamed as tokens with no retraction (no call was finalised), so a re-run's answer would run into it on screen and in the saved answer; making it disappear needs a new interim path (contract timing change). The honest line is simpler and holds the PO rule.

author: vera
text: scope:088a:gemini-answered: the runner sets TurnStats.answer_shown when non-blank answer text is streamed and clears it when that text is retracted as progress (interim); RetryingGemini re-runs an empty STOP only while it is False. Answer text only (the brief's rule): a chart with no text then an empty STOP still gets its re-run, which can only add the missing words. Whitespace never counts (BUG-008 too). _within: a chunk in hand is always passed on and the cut comes at the next wait (BUG-007); the 180 s counts only time spent waiting on the provider, not time the consumer holds a chunk (PERF-007).
